Driving Theory.question: When can you overtake on the left?
Driving Theory.answer: When the driver in front of you is turning right, when you intend to turn left.

Driving Theory.question: At an uncontrolled junction with roads of equal importance, to whom should you give way?
Driving Theory.answer: Give way to traffic on the right and proceed with caution.

Driving Theory.question: At a stop sign that has no white line, where should you stop?
What position would you take up for a right turn in a one way street?
How would you turn right on a main road?
Driving Theory.answer: Mirror and signal and the move into the right hand lane when clear, keeping left of the white line in the centre, proceeding when a suitable gap in traffic occurs, complete your turn, never cut corners and give way to pedestrians.

Driving Theory.question: How would you know a zebra crossing at night?
What does the island in the centre of a pedestrian crossing mean?
Driving Theory.answer: Each side of the island is a separate crossing.

Driving Theory.question: What restrictions are there in relation to the use of the horn?
Driving Theory.answer: It must not be used between the hours of 11:30 PM and 7:00 AM in a built up area, except in emergency.

Driving Theory.question: When driving at night when should you dip your headlights?
Driving Theory.answer: When meeting oncoming traffic, when following close behind another vehicle, on continuously lit roads.

Driving Theory.question: What should you do if dazzled by lights of an oncoming car?
Driving Theory.answer: Low down and stop if necessary.

Driving Theory.question: What is a clearway?
Driving Theory.answer: Stopping or parking are prohibited (except by buses and taxis) for the period of time indicated on the sign.

Driving Theory.question: What does a broken yellow line mean?
Driving Theory.answer: A broken yellow line marks the edge of the road.

Driving Theory.question: What does a single yellow line mean?
What is the legal parking distance from the kerb?
How close to a junction can you park?
Where should you not park?
Driving Theory.answer: Near a bend, the brow of a hill, a hump back bridge, a continuous white line, where your vehicle would obstruct traffic, opposite another vehicle, on a narrow road or a taxi rank.

Driving Theory.question: Where should you not overtake?
Driving Theory.answer: At a bend, a junction, brow of a hill, a hump back bridge, a continuous white line or anywhere your view is obstructed.

Driving Theory.question: What is the two second rule?
Driving Theory.answer: Stay two seconds behind the car in front. Use a stationary object on the road, start counting when the car should pass after continuing two seconds.

Driving Theory.question: If you saw a red triangle on the road, what would it mean?
Driving Theory.answer: That there an obstruction on the road ahead.

Driving Theory.question: What is the sequence of traffic lights?
At an uncontrolled junction, who has the right of way?
Driving Theory.answer: Take it that no one has the right of way and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

Driving Theory.question: What does a green light mean?
What does an amber light mean?
Driving Theory.answer: Stop, unless you are too close to stop safely.

Driving Theory.question: Name three people in authority for whom you must stop.
Driving Theory.answer: A Garda, a school warden or a person, a person in charge of animals, a flag man.

Driving Theory.question: If you were entering a one way street at the NO ENTRY end, what road markings would you see?
Driving Theory.answer: A continuous white line with a broken white line behind it.

Driving Theory.question: When can you cross a continuous line?
Driving Theory.answer: To avoid an obstruction, for access, or if there is a broken white line on your side of the road.

Driving Theory.question: a) What is the speed limit on a national primary road? b) What is the motorway speed limit?
Driving Theory.answer: a) Coach: 100 km/h, Truck: 80 km/h, Car: 100 km/h b) Coach: 100 km/h, Truck: 90km/h, Car: 120 km/h

Driving Theory.question: What rules apply to a junction box?
Driving Theory.answer: You cannot enter unless your way ahead is clear, with the exception of turning right.

Driving Theory.question: If there are two sets of white lines in the centre of the road, one continuous and one broken, which one would you obey?
Driving Theory.answer: The line on my side of the road.

Driving Theory.question: What do two sets of broken white lines in the centre of the road mean?
Driving Theory.answer: There will be one or two continuous white lines ahead.

Driving Theory.question: What does a broken white line in the centre of the road mean?
Driving Theory.answer: You may overtake if it is safe to do so.

Driving Theory.question: What do horizontal lines in the centre of the road mean?
Driving Theory.answer: You use them as a traffic island – you do NOT enter.

Driving Theory.question: What is the procedure for checking your oil?
Driving Theory.answer: The car must be on a flat surface and the engine must be half an hour cold. You take out the dip stick, you wipe it clean, put it back in again, take it out again, and the level should be between minimum and maximum. (Top up if needed.)

Driving Theory.question: How would you check your wheels and tires?
Driving Theory.answer: Check the tire depth by squeezing your finger into the tire crease. The minimum tire depth is 1,6 millimetres. Then, we do a visual check of the tire wall to make sure there are no screws, cuts, bulges and check that all the bolts are in place. Lastly, check if there is any air in the tire.

Driving Theory.question: How would you check if indicators and break lights are working?
Driving Theory.answer: Put everything on and walk around the car. To check the break lights, I ask someone to press the brake or reverse close to a wall, press the breaks and the wall will reflect the light.
